I'm sorting the rest of the candidates into specific diseases or disease classes. Thrombocytopenia reads as a broad category that covers several conditions, so I'm labeling it a disease class.

I'm settling on "X linked recessive thrombocytopenic disorder" as a specific disease, since the paper treats it as one entity, and I'm also leaning toward Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome being specific.

I'm checking the remaining candidates against the guidelines: "immune deficiencies" reads as a general term, so I'm leaving it out. "WAS" appears three times, and in "the classical WAS phenotype" it works as a modifier of "phenotype," which I'm still weighing.

Now I'm settling the WAS mentions: the one in "the classical WAS phenotype" and the one in "the WAS gene" both have WAS working as a modifier of a noun, so they count as modifiers rather than disease names. The parenthetical "Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome (WAS)" is an abbreviation definition, so that one stays a specific disease.

I'm checking whether "the gene for the Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome" counts as a modifier. Here the disease name is the object of "gene for," not a noun it modifies, so I'm keeping it as a specific disease.

I'm going through the remaining candidates: "thrombocytopenia" in the early-childhood sentence looks like a class of conditions, so I'm weighing that as a disease class, while the "X linked recessive thrombocytopenia" in the family's presentation reads as a specific entity.

I'm settling the rest of the candidates: "immunological abnormalities" and "immune deficiencies" are general terms, so I'm leaving both out.
